sources: dossier=Required behaviors (instance_killed arms, 2026-05-28 artifact) + Intentional absences ('instance_killed arms for fresh/stale — deliberately narrowed away') say the accept-set is exactly running+parked, fresh/stale/held excluded; doc=lines 13/43 say accepted only from running/parked, rejected from stale; code=state.go NextState accepts instance_killed->Failed from Pending(68-69), Stale(83-84), Running(102-103), Held(111-112), Parked(120-121), exhaustively table-tested in state_test.go:46-77 across all 17 reasons x 7 states.
note: Code (tested, exhaustive transition table) accepts instance_killed from five states, but the dossier's only intent record for this exact question is artifact-only (2026-05-28) and explicitly says the accept-set is narrowed to exactly running+parked — the opposite of current code. This is a genuine dossier-vs-code conflict, not simple doc drift. Question for human: did the seven-state redesign (2026-06-20, which absorbed held) and a later untracked change intentionally widen instance_killed to pending/stale/held, or has the state machine regressed past the deliberate 2026-05-28 narrowing and needs reverting to running/parked-only?

sources: dossier=Net position 'The audit-write role is split... non-signal transitions... keep writing the TransitionReason kind' (2026-05-23/2026-05-11, both artifact-tier); doc=Purpose role 2 / Boundaries claim non-signal transitions write audit rows keyed by reason.Kind; code=enforceAndUpdate (postgres nodes.go 286-354, sqlite mirror) issues no events.* call at all — verified no 'events.' reference in nodes.go; OperationalKind enum (kinds.go 80-125) has no dispatch_claimed/pure_cascade/acquire_pass/deadline_resume/auto_terminal_*/child_transitioned members, and the strings that do exist (e.g. fan_out_dispatched) differ from the matching reason kind (fanout_dispatched); KindStateTransition() (kinds.go:159) is referenced only in a conformance fixture and a unit test, never in production code paths.
note: Artifact-only dossier claim ('split audit model') directly contradicts concept:signal, a live design-corpus artifact stating the signal vocabulary unified the historical transition-reason-as-audit-surface away, and is refuted by code (no audit row is ever written by the state-update path). Per the provenance gate this is artifact-only AND design-incoherent (contradicts concept:signal) — flagging suspect-canonization. Question for human: is TransitionReason's audit-kind role (Purpose #2) fully retired in favor of the separate OperationalKind enum and signal type-paths, or does the dossier's 'split model' reflect an intended-but-unimplemented design that code should be brought into line with?

sources: dossier=Net position line 11 (split audit-write role, artifact-tier, same lineage as 725); design-corpus=concept:signal 'What it is'/'Purpose' — 'The signal vocabulary unifies the historical parallel surfaces (run outcome, transition reason, subscription's structured-filter fields) into one type-path-plus-payload contract' and 'Every signal writes one row to the persisted audit-event ledger with the event kind set to the signal's type-path'; doc=Purpose role 2 and Boundaries retain the pre-unification 'signal-bearing vs non-signal, reason-kind-as-audit-identity' model; code=confirms no reason-kind-keyed audit writes exist (see 725).
note: Same underlying conflict as 725: an artifact-only, uncorroborated dossier line asserts a still-live 'split' audit model that a currently-maintained sibling concept doc (concept:signal) explicitly describes as unified away, and code matches concept:signal not the dossier. Design-incoherent artifact-only claim -> design-call, suspect-canonization. Same human question as 725: retire the parallel audit-surface model from transition-reason.md, or is signal.md the one that's ahead of a still-intended split model?

sources: dossier=same 2026-05-28 artifact-tier entry as 724 ('exactly running->failed and parked->failed arms'), which excludes held as well as running/parked; doc=lines 13/43 name only running/parked as the resource-holding accept-set; code=killStates={running,parked,held} (instances.go:657-661) and NextState accepts instance_killed from Held (state.go:111-112); held is grouped with running/parked as the claim-holding set by IsSerializationGated (state.go:177-183).
note: Bundled into the same design-call as 724 — held's inclusion is part of the disputed accept-set question, not a separable clean fix: the dossier's stated intent excludes held too, so 'add held to the doc' cannot be applied without first resolving whether the widened accept-set (matching current tested code) or the narrow 2026-05-28 intent is authoritative. Deferred to the same human question posed in row 724.

sources: dossier=silent on settling_signal_type; doc=line 13 said the per-node update writes 'run-row state only, with no audit row'; code=force-terminate passes sig='terminal/error/instance_killed' (instances.go:695-697) and enforceAndUpdate stamps settling_signal_type=COALESCE($3,...) on the run row (nodes.go:339-347); test=test/scenarios/lifecycle_force_terminate_fullstack_test.go:65 asserts the force-failed run carries the instance_killed settling signal.

sources: dossier=Net position line 9, transcript-tier (2026-06-23): 'TransitionReason is a closed enum of exactly 17 real values... no free-form runtime additions'; doc=Purpose section line 22 lists 'policy-retry' among signal-bearing reasons; code=state.go var block enumerates exactly 17 ReasonXxx constants (GateCleared, DispatchClaimed, PolicyGiveUp, PureCascade, DispatchImpossible, AcquirePass, HandlerComplete, HandlerHeld, FanoutDispatched, HandlerPass, HandlerPark, AutoTerminalCommit, AutoTerminalAbandon, DeadlineResume, ParkTimeout, ChildTransitioned, InstanceKilled) with no PolicyRetry.
note: Transcript-tier claim of exactly 17 values is directly corroborated by an independent count of the Go constants (exactly 17, no policy_retry). Removed 'policy-retry' from the signal-bearing-reasons list in Purpose.

sources: dossier=Net position line 12: 'The node-run creation-reason enum is a distinct closed set: cascade, operator_invalidate, recalculate, message_delivery'; design-corpus=concept:node-run line 25 owns the creation-reason field with the identical four values; doc=line 13 said transition reason 'is distinct from... the operator reset/invalidate reasons' as if such transition reasons exist; code=state.go defines CreationReason (189-194) as a separate type from TransitionReason, with no operator-reset/operator-invalidate TransitionReason anywhere.
note: Dossier and concept:node-run agree the referenced value belongs to the distinct creation-reason enum, not a transition reason. Reworded the closing sentence to name the creation-reason field's operator_invalidate value via concept:node-run instead of implying a phantom transition reason.
